Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Do you mean any of the following: {'get_code_snippet(org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinter.print(java.lang.Object, java.lang.CharSequence, int, int))', 'get_code_snippet(org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinter.print(java.lang.Object))'}?"}

Diagnosis:
The failing test demonstrates that using CSVFormat.withHeader with CSVPrinter does not result in the header being printed out as expected. The current bug report explains that withHeader is only supported by CSVParser, not CSVPrinter, meaning the CSVPrinter does not inherently print headers based on the format's header setting.

Looking at CSVFormat.withHeader(java.lang.String...) shows it simply stores the header strings in the CSVFormat instance by passing them to the CSVFormat constructor. The CSVFormat constructor validates no duplicates exist and stores the header array internally.

Examining the CSVPrinter constructor shows that it simply stores the CSVFormat instance and validates it, but no indication it automatically prints the header row when a header is configured in the format.

The CSVPrinter printRecord and print methods handle printing values but do not check or print the header from the format. There's no call to print the header row independently.

The absence of CSVPrinter code to print the header from CSVFormat.withHeader explains why the test fails: the header row "C1,C2,C3" is never printed, only the data records are printed. The expected behavior that CSVPrinter support printing the headers from CSVFormat.withHeader does not currently exist, which matches the current bug report's description.

Recent bug reports on CSVFormat with header-related issues mostly relate to parser-side handling or format string generation. They do not indicate any existing implementation of printing headers in CSVPrinter or fix for this feature.

Hence, the root cause is that CSVPrinter does not implement printing headers automatically when CSVFormat has a header defined, despite CSVFormat holding the header information. This leads to testHeader failing to see the header row in the output.

Suggested fix: implement support in CSVPrinter to print the header row if CSVFormat has a header configured, before printing any records. This could be done in the constructor or before the first record is printed.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
